title: Germany election – shock for the country

paragraphs: The far-right AfD party won a big victory in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. It got almost 44% of the vote. The traditional CDU party lost more than half of its supporters.

Many voters chose the AfD because they were angry with the national government and worried about issues like migration and the economy. The AfD now holds 39 seats in the state parliament, which is just three seats short of an absolute majority.
Other political parties usually do not want to work with the AfD because of its extreme ideas, but forming a stable government without the AfD will be very difficult.

paragraphs: A far-right political party called the AfD wins a big election in Germany. Almost half of the people vote for them.
Many voters are unhappy with the old government. They want big changes. The AfD gets 39 seats in the local parliament. They need just three more seats to rule the state alone.
Other political parties do not want to work with the AfD. They think that its ideas are dangerous. Now, forming a new government in the state will be very hard for everyone.

words.d: a political group with very extreme, nationalist ideas
the group of people who rule a country

paragraphs: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party achieved a historic victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. It won 43.8% of the vote and secured 39 of the 83 parliamentary seats.
The ruling conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) suffered a major defeat when it dropped to just 17%.

Although the AfD fell three seats short of an absolute majority, its massive win has caused significant political turbulence across Germany. Experts point to voter dissatisfaction with the federal government, concerns over migration, and the popularity of local candidates as drivers of the AfD’s success. The election places immense pressure on the CDU’s policy that strictly prohibits cooperation with the far right.

With traditional coalition building extremely complicated, the AfD is actively attempting to persuade individual lawmakers to defect. If the AfD influences the state government, it plans radical policy changes regarding education, culture, and migration enforcement.

words.d: a state of confusion, violence, or unstable movement
to leave one group, country, or political party to join an opposing one
